children: rose 2.94% intraday after Bloomberg reported that the company plans to invest more than 1 billion ($1.16 billion) to build a new van at its Hordain plant in northern France, citing people familiar with the situation. The money covers upgrades at the existing site plus research and development elsewhere in France. Stellantis declined to comment.
Some work moves back inside the company. Suppliers currently handle parts of the process that Stellantis expects to take on itself, leaning on automation to make Hordain run more efficiently.

It fits a pattern under Antonio Filosa, who took over just over a year ago. He committed more than 1 billion earlier this year to three new electric and hybrid Peugeot models at Mulhouse from 2029, and last month promised to keep all 12 of the company's French sites open. Stellantis is targeting 6 billion of annual savings by 2028 while working through overcapacity, with partnerships with Leapmotor and Dongfeng intended to fill under-used plants in Rennes and Spain. The Pro One commercial vehicle unit plans 11 new or revamped models by 2030.

title: Stellantis Puts Another 1 Billion Into a French Plant
